purpose: Make full-scope mapping a pre-authoring thinking tool that exposes coverage, evidence, representation use, and template-driven repetition without treating repetition itself as a defect.
required_for: Any build spanning multiple items, sections, forms, or resource instances where the builder is authoring new learning/evidence content rather than merely rendering an already-finalized canonical set.
pre_authoring_gate: Map exact I-can / learning targets across the complete requested scope before final student materials are authored.
Map the intended learning/evidence job, representation/data/phenomenon/model use, and student reasoning/action that actually matters for each planned item/resource.
Read the complete map as a whole and repair accidental coverage gaps, unsupported overconcentration, or suspicious template clusters before rendering.
purposeful_repetition: Keep repetition when it serves a mapped purpose such as fluency, retrieval, repeated independent evidence, consistent comparison across forms, repeated use of a high-value representation, or deliberate return to an important structure.
accidental_repetition: Flag repetition when the same question shell, experience sequence, representation choice, reasoning suffix, or student action recurs mainly because it is easy to template/render rather than because the learning architecture calls for it.
decision_rule: When repetition looks suspicious, ask what mapped learning/evidence purpose it serves. If the purpose is real, keep it. If the repetition is only a template byproduct, revise the PLAN before authoring final resources.
no_quota_rule: Do not impose anti-repetition quotas such as 'no structure more than twice.' The goal is intentionality, not maximum variety.
late_audit_distinction: This pre-authoring map review is NOT a late anti-clone/diversification pass. After authoring, do not launch broad cosmetic rewrites merely to lower repetition; repair actual alignment, security, evidence, representation, or quality defects.
course_specific_reflection: Repeated derivative/integral/limit families may intentionally recur when the Assessment Plan calls for procedural fluency or repeated independent evidence.
Use the map to see whether graphical, numerical, analytical, and verbal work is actually present where the I-cans call for it; do not rotate representations merely to satisfy a quota.
AP-style task/scoring structures may recur when authentic, but one scaffold or stock justification frame should not become the generator default across unrelated targets.
